record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; source code and full logs were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says it tried to replicate refusal-vector ablation and reports behavioral results for two instruction-tuned models.
record.gate_note: The README reports ablation outcomes for Qwen and Llama. The JSON-format prompt-injection result is not a row: it does not test suppression of the refusal direction or refusal of harmful user requests. The layer-selection scan is mentioned but no result from it is reported.
record.test_reason: The README tries to replicate difference-in-means refusal-direction removal on two models used in the original paper (Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat and Llama-3-8B-Instruct). It reports JailbreakBench refusal rates before and after. The recipe differs from the original: subtraction at strength 1.5x at layer 14 only, not projection ablation at every layer and position.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that naive linear ablation gave a null result in Qwen, suggesting its safety features are stored non-linearly or are not localized at the tested layer. In Llama-3, ablation removed refusals but caused manic positivity and incoherence, suggesting safety is entangled with tone. They add that safety varies by architecture and can be bypassed externally via JSON formatting constraints.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a difference-in-means refusal direction and subtraction, but reports intervention at Layer 14 rather than ablation at every layer and position. The README also proposes paired prompts to reduce grammatical confounds. Repository type: experimental project/replication attempt.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differed between Qwen and Llama. The README also reports that the initial broad-prompt direction produced gibberish in Qwen, whereas the later JBB refusal-rate result was a null result.

fits_no_version.finding: In an indirect prompt injection, a JSON formatting constraint led Qwen to leak a secret from its system prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Format-compliance pressure can override safety instructions in black-box use, independently of the refusal direction.

record.problems: The README labels the work a prototype and its metrics illustrative. Full logs are excluded; the automated refusal judge is Gemini 3. The initial Qwen output-quality result is qualitative, and the README does not clearly document whether the paired-prompt direction was the one used for every quantitative result. No controls or general-capability benchmark are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported ablation outcomes were omitted. The JSON-format attack result was left out because it does not test a listed claim version's refusal-direction behavior.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; projection ablation at every layer and position; quantitative capability benchmarks.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction, and no adversarial training against ablation.
No multi-direction, cone or affine comparison.
No separation of harmfulness from refusal.
No cross-language, variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
No comparison of training methods or stages.

missing.what: A qualitative statement that Qwen 'simply answered the harmful prompts (e.g., giving bomb recipes)' after ablation. This conflicts with the Qwen null result in r2 and is not recorded.
A layer-separation scan that selected layer 14; no per-layer results are given.

record.verdict_notes: This is a prototype repository; the README says its metrics are illustrative. The recipe deviates from the original: single-layer subtraction at 1.5x rather than all-layer projection ablation. It is unclear which direction (broad or paired-prompt) produced each quantitative result. Weigh these verdicts as weak evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction, ablating it at every layer and position, and systematic evaluation of other abilities were not tested.
No weight edit or released-model weight-edit evaluation is reported.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separation of harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions is tested.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.

relation.reason: The study reports its own before/after refusal rates and coherence outcomes under removal of the refusal direction.

tranche.reason: The direction is difference-in-means and the models and JailbreakBench set match the original. But the removal step is a single-layer (layer 14) subtraction at 1.5x, not projection at every layer and position. Refusal is judged by Gemini 3, not substring matching or Llama Guard 2. That is a different method and measure aimed at the same question. Borderline call.

source_check.notes: The README marks itself a prototype: AI-written code, unverified, metrics 'illustrative' only, logs withheld. It gives no control, no induction test and no capability benchmark. The §3.3 line 'Unlike Qwen, which simply answered the harmful prompts' sits oddly with the §1.4 Qwen null result, and the README does not say which direction the N=100 Qwen run used.
